places.name: Himeji, the white heron
places.narrative: Himeji Castle earns its white-heron nickname through more than its pale walls: its nested gates, angled paths and layered defenses make the approach feel like a story unfolding. From the station, the keep rises at the end of a broad avenue, but the details appear slowly: plastered storehouses, narrow passages and views framed through defensive openings. Cross into Koko-en and the mood changes from military architecture to ponds, tea houses and carefully composed gardens. The contrast is the reason to stay beyond a quick photograph. Spring blossoms frame the moat; autumn colour deepens the garden. Start early, wear shoes suited to steep wooden stairs, and allow a half-day rather than racing through the castle rooms.
places.access: From Himeji Station, walk the straight central avenue for about 20 minutes or take a local bus toward the castle. JR Sanyo Shinkansen stops at Himeji; Kansai International and Osaka Itami airports connect by rail or airport bus via Osaka. Cars can use signed paid city lots; the castle grounds are pedestrian. The Mt. Shosha ropeway and Engyoji require a separate bus journey from Himeji Station.
places.season: Spring brings cherry blossoms around the moat; summer is hot and humid, while autumn colours suit Koko-en. The castle is open year-round except temporary closures; heat, rain and busy holiday periods affect stair comfort and entry queues.
places.plan: Begin at the castle approach, tour the keep and Nishinomaru, then cross to Koko-en for a slower garden walk. Allow 4-6 hours, plus about half a day if adding Mt. Shosha and Engyoji. Castle stairs are steep; check the official site for entry limits and current hours.

contactSource.title: Himeji Castle official visitor information

places.stay: Stay near Himeji Station for shinkansen access and restaurants, or in the castle-side center for an early walk before tour groups arrive.
places.cost: Castle and Koko-en admission are ticketed; transport to Mt. Shosha, ropeway and temple admission are separate. Confirm current fees, entry hours and any maintenance closures before travel.
points: Himeji Station
Begin at the north exit and follow Otemae-dori toward the keep; the castle vista opens gradually.
Himeji Castle
Enter through the defensive gates, notice the layered paths, then climb the steep wooden stairways at a measured pace.
Koko-en Garden

Mt. Shosha and Engyoji

places.name: Koyasan after dusk
places.narrative: Koyasan is a living Buddhist mountain town, and its atmosphere comes from the relationship between its sacred sites rather than a single grand building. At Okunoin, stone memorials and towering cedars line a long approach to Kobo Daishi's mausoleum; lantern light and quiet voices make the walk especially memorable near dusk. In the daytime, Kongobuji's painted rooms and rock garden introduce the scale of Shingon Buddhism, while the vermilion Konpon Daito rises above Danjo Garan's temple precinct. Move slowly and treat the cemetery as a place of worship, not a theatrical set: photography restrictions apply near sacred areas. Sleep in a shukubo if you can, then hear the morning service before the mountain road and temple lanes grow busy.
places.access: From Osaka Namba, take the Nankai Koya Line to Gokurakubashi, then the cable car to Koyasan Station and a Nankai bus into town. The nearest airports are Kansai International and Osaka Itami, reached through Osaka rail connections. Driving uses mountain roads and limited parking; buses are more practical between temple districts. Confirm cable-car and bus service before setting out.
places.season: Spring and autumn offer comfortable walking and changing forest colour; winter can bring snow and service disruption. Okunoin is accessible year-round, but temple interiors have their own hours and sacred-area rules. Dusk visits require a return bus or a stay nearby.
places.plan: Visit Danjo Garan and Kongobuji in daylight, then walk the Ichinohashi-to-Okunoin approach before dusk. Allow 5-7 hours with bus transfers; staying overnight makes the morning service and cemetery walk unhurried. Keep voices low and obey photography signs.

contactSource.title: Koya Tourism Association visitor information

places.stay: Choose a temple lodging in central Koyasan for a morning service and easy bus access, or stay near Senjuinbashi for meals and transport connections.
places.cost: Temple entry, museums, cable car and local transport have separate fares. Cemetery paths are free; lodging and meals vary by temple. Check current temple admission and transport timetables.

Okunoin

Kongobuji Temple

Danjo Garan

places.name: Kumano Kodo, the old paths
places.narrative: The Kumano Kodo is not a single scenic walk but a network of pilgrimage routes linking sacred sites across the Kii Peninsula. For a first encounter, the Nakahechi approach from Takijiri-oji reveals why the path has drawn pilgrims for centuries: the modern road falls away, stone steps rise into cedar forest, and small oji shrines punctuate the climb. This is a serious mountain trail, with roots, uneven stones and steep sections; the classic journey to Kumano Hongu Taisha takes multiple days and should not be improvised as a day trip. Begin with the pilgrimage center's maps, check bus times, carry water and rain layers, and book accommodation ahead. Walking only a manageable segment still gives the route its proper texture without pretending the whole pilgrimage fits into one afternoon.
places.access: Take the JR Kuroshio limited express to Kii-Tanabe Station, then the Ryujin bus to Takijiri-oji, about 40 minutes. Nanki-Shirahama Airport is the closest regional airport; Osaka Kansai is a longer rail journey. Cars can reach trailheads, but parking and one-way trail logistics need planning. Use official bus schedules and arrange luggage transfer and overnight stays before hiking.
places.season: Spring and autumn are generally more comfortable for hiking. Summer brings heat, humidity and heavy rain; winter days are shorter and mountain conditions can be cold. Trail and bus conditions change, so check current official alerts and daylight before departure.
places.plan: For a first day, visit Takijiri-oji and the pilgrimage center, then hike only to a suitable booked overnight point such as Takahara if prepared. Allow 5-8 hours for trail walking, excluding transfers. The full Nakahechi is a multi-day hike; use official maps and do not rely on this schematic map for trail navigation.

contactSource.title: Tanabe City Kumano Tourism Bureau visitor information

places.stay: Book a minshuku or guesthouse in Takahara, Chikatsuyu or Hongu according to the stage you will actually hike; village accommodation is limited and reservations matter.
places.cost: Trail access is generally free; buses, luggage forwarding, guided walks and lodging are paid. Weather can affect transport and trail safety. Confirm current services and accommodation before travel.

Collect current bus and trail information at the station before boarding for the mountain trailhead.

places.name: Lake Biwa's eastern shore
places.narrative: On Lake Biwa's eastern shore, water, castle town and merchant streets make a rewarding route through Japan's largest lake basin. Hikone Castle still commands its hill above the water, with original timber interiors and a broad view from the keep; nearby Genkyuen Garden frames the castle across its pond. Farther north, Nagahama's old Kurokabe quarter tells a different story through merchant houses, glass studios and port history. These towns are connected by rail, not one continuous walking path, so treat the day as a sequence of compact visits. The lake's scale is easiest to appreciate from a harbor or ferry deck. Spring and autumn suit the outdoor sections; summer is humid and shoreline winds can change quickly. Build in train and boat time rather than trying to circle the lake in a day.
places.access: Use JR Hikone Station for the castle and JR Nagahama Station for the Kurokabe quarter; the JR Biwako Line links both towns. Osaka and Kyoto connect by rail, while Kansai International and Osaka Itami airports feed into those hubs. Driving uses the Meishin Expressway and town parking, but rail is easier for a two-town route. Lake cruises depart from specific ports and require timetable checks.
places.season: Spring cherry blossoms and autumn foliage frame Hikone Castle and lakeside walks. Summer is hot and humid; winter can be cold beside the water. Boat operations and museum hours vary by season, so confirm schedules before building a cross-shore itinerary.
places.plan: Spend a morning at Hikone Castle and Genkyuen, then take the JR Biwako Line north to Nagahama for Kurokabe Square and the port area. Allow 6-8 hours with train changes and museum time; a lake cruise or Chikubushima requires a separate boat timetable.

places.stay: Stay near Hikone Station for castle access or near Nagahama Station for a slower evening around the old town and lakefront.
places.cost: Hikone Castle and some museums charge admission; trains, boat trips, gardens and parking have separate costs. Check current tickets, cruise operations and opening hours.

places.name: Miyajima tide lines
places.narrative: Miyajima changes with the tide. At high water, Itsukushima Shrine and its great vermilion torii seem to float above the Seto Inland Sea; at low tide, visitors can walk across the exposed shore toward the gate. Check the tide chart before choosing your moment, then slow down in the shrine corridors, where the water, pillars and mountains create shifting reflections. Beyond the waterfront, Daisho-in's lantern stairways and small halls offer a quieter, lived-in spiritual landscape. Deer wander through the town, but they are wild animals and should not be fed. Stay after the day boats leave and the island becomes more intimate: lanterns glow, shop shutters close and the tide keeps changing the view. Respect shrine rules and keep the beach clean.
places.access: From Hiroshima Station, take the JR Sanyo Line to Miyajimaguchi, walk to the pier and ride either of the two regular ferries for about 10 minutes. Hiroshima Airport connects to Hiroshima Station by airport bus; Iwakuni Airport is another regional option. Drivers can park near Miyajimaguchi, but cars on the island are unnecessary. Check ferry timetables and tide charts for your visit date.
places.season: Spring and autumn are comfortable for island walks; summer is humid and winter can be windy on the water. The torii view depends on tide rather than season. Ferry services operate throughout the year but can be affected by severe weather.
places.plan: Time the shrine and torii for the tide you most want to see, then walk to Daisho-in and Momijidani Park. Allow 5-7 hours including the ferry, with extra time for Mt. Misen or an overnight stay. Follow shrine etiquette and protect food from deer.

contactSource.title: Miyajima Tourist Association access and contact

places.stay: Stay in Miyajima town for an early or evening shrine visit, or near Hiroshima Station for straightforward rail and ferry connections.
places.cost: Ferries, shrine entry, ropeway and museum visits have separate charges; the island itself is not a single ticketed attraction. Check current ferry fares and shrine hours.

places.name: Hiroshima, a city of peace
places.narrative: Hiroshima's Peace Memorial Park asks visitors to move from seeing to understanding. The A-Bomb Dome stands beside the river as a preserved witness to the destruction of August 1945, while the park's long axis leads toward the Cenotaph and the Peace Flame. The museum is emotionally demanding and deeply important; give it time, read the personal accounts and plan a quiet pause afterward. Across the river, central Hiroshima is a lively modern city whose everyday life makes the memorial landscape more powerful, not less. This is a place for reflection rather than quick sightseeing. Visit respectfully, keep voices low near memorials and avoid treating the site as a backdrop. Spring and autumn are comfortable for walking; hot summer days call for water and shade.
places.access: Hiroshima Station is served by the Sanyo Shinkansen and JR lines. From the station, take a Hiroshima Electric Railway tram or bus to the Peace Memorial Park area; Hiroshima Airport has limousine buses to the station. By car, use paid city garages and walk or ride transit into the park. The museum and dome are separated by a short pedestrian route.
places.season: The park is open throughout the year and spring or autumn offers comfortable walking. August 6 is a major remembrance day with large crowds; summer heat is intense. Museum schedules and special events can change, so check the city site before visiting.
places.plan: Begin at the A-Bomb Dome, cross into the park to the Cenotaph and Peace Flame, then spend unhurried time in the museum. Allow 4-6 hours and leave a quiet interval afterward. The museum is impactful and may be distressing; visitors can pace or pause the visit.

places.stay: Stay around Hiroshima Station for rail connections or Hondori and Kamiyacho for a central base within walking or tram distance of the park.
places.cost: The park is free and open continuously; the Peace Memorial Museum charges admission. Confirm current opening hours, admission and remembrance event arrangements.
points: A-Bomb Dome
View the preserved structure from the designated path and read the memorial context before photographing.

places.name: Tottori's shifting dunes
places.narrative: Tottori's dunes are a landscape in motion. Wind redraws the ridges every day, leaving ripples that seem to run toward the Sea of Japan; the climb to Umanose, the horse's back, rewards patient walkers with a wide horizon. The dunes belong to a protected coastal geopark, so stay on established routes and never write or carve into the sand. Nearby, the Sand Museum turns sand into immense temporary sculptures, adding a surprising indoor counterpoint to the open shore. Morning and late afternoon soften the light and reduce the heat underfoot. In summer, the sand can become dangerously hot; wear proper shoes, carry water and avoid a strenuous midday crossing. Check weather and activity operations before arrival, as wind and conditions can change the experience quickly.
places.access: From JR Tottori Station, take a local route bus to the Sakyu-kaikan or Sand Museum stops, around 20 minutes; weekend and holiday sightseeing buses also operate seasonally. Tottori Sand Dunes Conan Airport is about 20 minutes by car. The Tottori Expressway serves drivers, with signed parking near the dunes. Bus frequencies vary, so confirm return service before walking out onto the shore.
places.season: Spring and autumn are the most comfortable walking seasons. Summer sand gets extremely hot and requires shoes, water and shade breaks; winter wind can be strong. Sand Museum exhibits change periodically and may close between installations.
places.plan: Start at the visitor center, cross the dunes toward Umanose and the sea, then visit the Sand Museum. Allow 3-5 hours with photo stops; add time for the geopark coast or local bus connections. Stay on marked paths, avoid writing in the sand and follow heat guidance.

contactSource.title: Visit Tottori City official dunes guide

places.stay: Stay near Tottori Station for restaurants and bus access, or choose a coastal property if you want sunrise or sunset at the dunes.
places.cost: The dunes are free; the Sand Museum, parking and optional activities have separate fees. Confirm current exhibit dates and activity availability, which may change with weather.
points: Sand Dunes Visitor Center

Tottori Sand Museum

Sand Dunes Conan Airport viewpoint

places.name: Kurashiki's canal quarter
places.narrative: Kurashiki's Bikan quarter was shaped by trade, and the white storehouses beside the canal still make that history visible. Willow branches soften the waterline; black-and-white namako walls, latticed facades and old merchant homes reveal the district one lane at a time. A traditional boat ride offers a low view of the canal, but tickets and operating hours can be limited, so reserve or check early. The Ohara Museum brings Western art into the same compact neighborhood, while Ivy Square repurposes a red-brick textile mill as a place to wander and rest. Come early for quiet reflections, then stay into evening when the historic streets glow. The Bikan area is lived-in, not a stage: keep voices low and respect private doorways and residents.
places.access: Walk about 10-15 minutes from JR Kurashiki Station to the Bikan area; the station connects to JR Okayama and Shin-Kurashiki. Okayama Airport links to the city by bus. Drivers can use municipal parking near the quarter, but the historic lanes are best explored on foot. Facility hours and closures differ, especially on Mondays and holidays.
places.season: The quarter is attractive year-round; spring and autumn are comfortable for walking, while summer is humid. Evening landscape lighting is seasonal and museum or boat hours vary. Check the boat counter early and verify individual museum opening days.
places.plan: Start along the canal before crowds, visit the Ohara Museum, then walk through Ivy Square and the preserved Honmachi lanes. Allow 4-6 hours. Boat tickets may sell out or run to limited schedules; keep the district walkable and avoid blocking residents' doorways.

contactSource.title: Okayama official guide: Kurashiki Bikan Quarter

places.stay: Stay near Kurashiki Station for rail access or in a licensed historic-quarter inn for a quieter evening after day visitors leave.
places.cost: Street walks are free; boat rides, museums and some historic buildings charge admission. Confirm current prices, Monday closures and boat ticket availability.
points: Kurashiki Station
Walk south from the station toward the historic district; allow time for a calm arrival through the modern center.
Kurashiki Canal
Follow the willow-lined water and white storehouses; check boat times early if you want the traditional canal ride.
Ohara Museum of Art
Explore the museum's collection and architecture; check current hours and photography rules before entry.
Kurashiki Ivy Square

places.name: Onomichi's hillside lanes
places.narrative: Onomichi is a port town layered up a hillside, where temple roofs, narrow stairways and glimpses of the Seto Inland Sea appear between ordinary homes. The Senkoji Ropeway lifts visitors above the slope, but the more memorable descent is on foot through the Path of Literature, past small temples and old stone walls. At the waterfront, ferries and cargo vessels animate the narrow channel between Honshu and Mukaishima. Onomichi's scale rewards pauses: look back from a landing, step into a quiet temple courtyard, and watch the light change across the islands. The route includes steep stairs and uneven lanes, so comfortable shoes matter. Spring cherry blossoms draw crowds to Senkoji Park; other seasons bring clear views and gentler walks. Keep residential lanes quiet and do not enter private property for photographs.
places.access: JR Onomichi Station is on the Sanyo Main Line; Shin-Onomichi Shinkansen Station is inland and connects by local bus or taxi. Hiroshima Airport has buses toward Onomichi. Drivers can use waterfront parking, but the hillside route is on foot. The ropeway base and station are reached from the central town; confirm operating hours and weather conditions.
places.season: Spring blossoms at Senkoji Park are popular; autumn and clear winter days offer broad island views. Summer is hot and humid. Ropeway operations and temple opening hours may vary with weather and events.
places.plan: Ride or walk up to Senkoji Park, descend via the Path of Literature and hillside temples, then finish along the waterfront at Onomichi U2. Allow 4-6 hours for stairs, viewpoints and café breaks. Use the ropeway if steep climbs are difficult and check return transport.

contactSource.title: Onomichi tourism visitor information

places.stay: Stay near Onomichi Station or the waterfront for easy rail access, ferries and an early start before the hillside lanes get busy.
places.cost: The hillside walk is free; ropeway rides, museums and temple interiors may charge. Confirm operating days, ropeway hours and museum admission before travel.

Onomichi U2 waterfront

places.name: Izumo, land of old stories
places.narrative: Izumo Taisha invites a slower kind of visit. Its immense shimenawa rope, broad shrine grounds and forested approach feel distinct from the dense urban shrines found elsewhere in Japan. The shrine is closely associated with stories of the kami and connections between people; its architecture and worship customs have their own character, so follow posted guidance rather than assuming familiar rituals apply. Nearby, the Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo places the shrine within a deeper regional history, and Inasa Beach gives the coast a mythic edge at sunset. The three make a satisfying day when linked by local bus or taxi. Spring and autumn are pleasant; summer heat can make the open grounds tiring. Allow time for the museum and approach, and keep the sacred precinct calm.
places.access: From JR Izumo-shi Station, take an Ichibata Bus to the shrine area in about 25 minutes or use the Ichibata Railway to Izumo Taisha-mae Station and walk. Izumo Enmusubi Airport has shuttle buses to JR Izumo-shi Station; flights connect with Tokyo and Osaka. By car, use the signed shrine parking. Local bus frequency is limited compared with city transit, so check return times.
places.season: The shrine is open year-round; spring and autumn are comfortable for the long approach and beach. Summer is hot and the grounds are exposed. Seasonal ceremonies can affect access, so check the shrine calendar and museum schedule.
places.plan: Walk the shrine approach and grounds first, then visit the Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo before continuing to Inasa Beach. Allow 5-7 hours including local transfers. Return buses are less frequent than urban services; confirm the schedule before walking to the coast.

contactSource.title: Izumo Taisha official access and contact

places.stay: Stay near JR Izumo-shi Station for transport connections or around the shrine for an early visit and a quieter coastal evening.
places.cost: The main shrine grounds are free; museum entry, transport and some special areas may cost. Confirm event schedules and current museum admission.
points: Izumo Taisha-mae Station

places.name: Iwami Ginzan's forest paths
places.narrative: Iwami Ginzan is a cultural landscape where a former silver mine, a preserved town and mountain forest belong to one story. Begin at the World Heritage Center to understand the mine's scale and plan transport: private vehicles do not serve the historic core, and buses or walking connect the dispersed sites. Omori's narrow street follows the river past merchant houses, temples and small workshops. Beyond town, the path toward Ryugenji Mabu enters a quiet valley where the mine tunnel makes the labor and engineering tangible. This is a place to notice how nature reclaimed the industrial landscape, not just to collect a heritage-site stamp. The walking distances are substantial, buses limited and some terrain uneven. Visit in spring or autumn, start early, and check mine access and shuttle availability before setting out.
places.access: Travel by JR Sanin Main Line to Odashi Station, then take the local bus to Iwami Ginzan World Heritage Center, roughly 25-35 minutes depending on service. Izumo Airport is the nearest major regional airport; buses and trains connect onward. Drivers should park at the Heritage Center and use public buses or walk into Omori. Services are infrequent, so plan the return carefully.
places.season: Spring and autumn offer the most comfortable walking. Summer is humid and rainy; winter can bring cold conditions and reduced services. Ryugenji Mabu and shuttle operations have specific schedules and may close for weather or maintenance.
places.plan: Orient at the World Heritage Center, take the bus to Omori, walk the historic town and continue toward Ryugenji Mabu only if time and mobility allow. Allow 5-7 hours. The mine trail adds a significant round trip; confirm shuttle operation and last bus before starting.

contactSource.title: Iwami Ginzan World Heritage Center access

places.stay: Stay in Omori for a quiet heritage-town evening, Yunotsu for hot springs, or Oda City near Odashi Station for practical transport.
places.cost: World Heritage Center exhibits, mine entry, buses and parking have separate costs. Most town streets and forest paths are free. Confirm current mine opening and bus timetables.

places.name: The Iya Valley
places.narrative: The Iya Valley folds deep into Shikoku's mountains, where roads cling to cliffs above the emerald Iya River and hamlets appear on steep slopes. The vine bridge at Kazurabashi is the best-known crossing, but its appeal lies in its setting: woven vines, rushing water and forested walls compress the senses into a brief, exhilarating passage. Nearby, Biwa Falls and the small settlement are best explored slowly, while the Peeing Boy statue offers a dramatic roadside viewpoint farther along the gorge. These places are not a continuous footpath; narrow roads and sparse buses make transport choices central to the day. A rental car gives flexibility, but mountain driving takes concentration. Spring green and autumn colour are lovely; rain can make paths slick. Check bus returns and bridge operating conditions before descending into the valley.
places.access: From JR Oboke Station, Shikoku Kotsu buses reach Kazurabashi in about 20 minutes when services operate. Takamatsu Airport is the most useful air gateway, with onward bus and rail connections; Tokushima Airport is another option. Drivers use National Route 32 and mountain roads, with limited parking at viewpoints. Bus service is sparse, so confirm the timetable and do not assume attractions are walk-connected.
places.season: Spring and autumn are especially scenic; summer is humid and rain can swell the river. Winter may bring snow, road restrictions and seasonal closures. The vine bridge can close in bad weather or for maintenance; check the operator on the day.
places.plan: Use Oboke Station as the transport hub, visit Kazurabashi and Biwa Falls, then add the Peeing Boy viewpoint only with a car or suitable bus connection. Allow 5-7 hours including mountain transfers. Roads are narrow; keep daylight and weather in mind.

contactSource.title: Tokushima Tourism: Vine Bridges of Iya Valley

places.stay: Stay around Oboke for rail and river access, or in a valley onsen inn near Kazurabashi to avoid rushing the last bus back.
places.cost: Kazurabashi charges an entry fee; buses, parking, river activities and lodging are separate. Check current bridge hours, weather closures and transport fares.

places.name: Naoshima, art and sea
places.narrative: Naoshima's art is inseparable from its island setting. A bright pumpkin beside the port can feel playful, while Chichu Art Museum turns natural light into part of the work itself. The island's quiet roads, fishing hamlets and sea views connect installations and museums, but distances are longer than they look on a map. Reserve timed museum entry well ahead, especially for Chichu, and plan around ferry and local bus schedules. Benesse House blends art, architecture and accommodation; visitors should follow its photography and access rules. The best day leaves space between venues rather than treating the island as a checklist. Spring and autumn bring comfortable cycling weather; summer heat and ferry crowds require planning. Respect residents and do not photograph private homes. End at the port as the light fades over the Inland Sea.
places.access: Ferries to Naoshima's Miyanoura Port run from Uno Port in Okayama and Takamatsu Port in Kagawa. Uno is reached by JR from Okayama; Takamatsu has rail, airport bus and domestic flights. Cars can use some island roads, but parking is limited and bicycles or local buses suit most visitors. Museum access may require advance reservation; check port-specific ferry schedules.
places.season: Spring and autumn are comfortable for cycling and outdoor art. Summer is hot, with busy ferries; winter schedules and museum closures can differ. Many art facilities close on set weekdays or between exhibitions, so check the official calendar and reserve timed tickets.
places.plan: Arrive at Miyanoura, see the port-side art, then take the island bus or bicycle to Chichu and the Benesse area. Allow 6-8 hours and reserve museum slots before buying transport. Leave time for ferry queues and the return crossing.
places.contact: Benesse Art Site Naoshima visitor information

contactSource.title: Benesse Art Site Naoshima: Chichu Art Museum

places.stay: Stay near Miyanoura for ferry convenience or book a Benesse-area stay well in advance for an immersive art-focused visit.
places.cost: Museum admissions and timed reservations are paid; ferries, buses, bike rentals and lodging are separate. Confirm current prices and access rules; some installations are outdoors while museums may restrict photography.
points: Miyanoura Port
Arrive by the ferry you booked or checked; the port area has public art and island transport connections.
Red Pumpkin
See Yayoi Kusama's port-side work in its outdoor setting and follow posted rules around the installation.
Chichu Art Museum
Reserve a timed ticket, arrive for your slot and follow strict photography and visitor instructions inside.
Benesse House Museum
Continue by local bus or bicycle through the art-and-sea landscape; verify which facilities admit day visitors.

places.name: Matsuyama's castle hill
places.narrative: Matsuyama Castle still crowns the city's central hill, and the climb reveals why this is more than a photogenic skyline. The surviving keep and connected towers show how a defensive complex could occupy a compact mountaintop, while the view opens across Matsuyama toward the sea. Ride the ropeway or chairlift for an easier ascent, then explore the castle grounds at walking pace. Below, Ninomaru Historical Garden traces the former castle residence and offers a quieter way back into town. From there, the streetcar connects to Dogo Onsen, making a satisfying second chapter rather than an unrelated add-on. Spring blossoms and autumn foliage frame the hill; summer heat is tiring on the slopes. Castle access may involve steep stairs, so check accessibility and wear stable shoes.
places.access: Matsuyama Station connects by JR to other parts of Shikoku; Matsuyama Airport has buses to the city center. From JR Matsuyama Station, take the streetcar to Okaido and walk to the ropeway street. Drivers can use the castle parking area, but cars cannot reach the mountaintop. Dogo Onsen is linked by tram, not a direct walk from the castle.
places.season: Spring cherry blossoms and autumn foliage make the hill especially attractive. Summer is hot and humid, while winter can be brisk. Castle hours, ropeway service and chairlift operations vary seasonally and may pause for weather.
places.plan: Take the ropeway or chairlift to the castle, explore the keep and grounds, descend toward Ninomaru Historical Garden and finish with a streetcar ride to Dogo Onsen if time allows. Allow 4-6 hours for castle and garden, longer with Dogo. Confirm last ropeway times.

contactSource.title: Ehime official Matsuyama Castle guide

places.stay: Stay near Okaido for easy castle access, or in Dogo Onsen for a bathhouse-centered evening with a short streetcar connection to the city center.
places.cost: The keep charges admission; ropeway and chairlift fares are separate, as are gardens and Dogo facilities. Check current seasonal hours and closures.
points: Okaido tram stop
Use the city tram for the central approach; walk through the castle town toward the ropeway street.
Matsuyama Castle ropeway
Choose ropeway or chairlift for the ascent; follow current operation notices and do not drive to the hilltop.
Matsuyama Castle keep
Explore the surviving tower complex and panoramic views; interior stairs are steep and may be challenging.
Ninomaru Historical Garden
Descend to the former residence garden for a quieter finish before continuing by tram toward Dogo Onsen.

places.name: Shimanami Kaido by bicycle
places.narrative: The Shimanami Kaido turns island-hopping into a journey measured by bridges, citrus groves and sea crossings. The full signed cycling route links Onomichi and Imabari across about 70 kilometers, but beginners should not mistake that for an easy casual ride: bridge ramps climb, supplies are sparse on bridges, and weather matters. A more welcoming plan is to ride one section, stop on an island and stay overnight, then decide whether to continue. Mukaishima, Innoshima and Ikuchijima each have a different rhythm, from port lanes to bridge viewpoints and citrus orchards. Rent the right bicycle, check drop-off rules and plan the return before setting out. Spring and autumn are ideal; summer heat demands extra water. Follow the blue route markings, use ferries where advised, and leave room for spontaneous seaside breaks.
places.access: Start from JR Onomichi Station or Sunrise Itoyama near Imabari; both are reached by rail and regional buses. Hiroshima and Matsuyama airports serve opposite ends of the route. The Onomichi-Mukaishima crossing is by ferry for cyclists; cars use the expressway and cannot follow every cycling access ramp. Rental terminals and one-way bike returns vary, so reserve and verify your endpoint transport.
places.season: Spring and autumn offer comfortable temperatures and clear sea views. Summer heat and humidity can be severe; winter brings wind and shorter daylight. Check bridge, ferry and rental operations, and avoid riding in unsafe weather.
places.plan: For a first outing, ride a shorter signed section from Onomichi via ferry to Mukaishima and onward toward Innoshima, then return using a confirmed ferry or overnight stay. The full 70 km usually takes 7-9 hours with breaks and suits prepared riders. Plan water and return transport first.

contactSource.title: JNTO National Cycle Route: Shimanami Kaido

places.stay: Stay in Onomichi for the Hiroshima-side start, Imabari near Sunrise Itoyama for an Ehime-side start, or book an island guesthouse to split the route.
places.cost: Bike rental, ferries, accommodation and some bridge tolls are separate costs. Check rental return policies, ferry bicycle charges, route closures and current toll details before departure.

Collect a suitable bike, helmet and route map; confirm drop-off rules before leaving the terminal.
Mukaishima ferry

places.name: Cape Ashizuri's ocean edge
places.narrative: At Cape Ashizuri, Shikoku seems to end in open water. The lighthouse stands above cliffs where the Pacific horizon stretches around the headland, and the coastal path alternates between exposed viewpoints and subtropical greenery. Nearby Kongofukuji Temple is the 38th temple on the Shikoku pilgrimage, adding a human and spiritual scale to the ocean spectacle. Walk the marked loop slowly; wind, spray and sudden rain can make exposed rock dangerous. The cape lies far from major rail hubs, so the journey is part of the visit rather than a quick detour. Spring and autumn bring more comfortable conditions, while summer is hot and typhoon season can disrupt travel. Stay overnight if possible, arrive with fuel and supplies, and let the last light linger over the sea.
places.access: From Nakamura Station on the Tosa Kuroshio Railway, local buses take roughly 1 hour 40 minutes to the cape; check the sparse timetable carefully. Kochi Ryoma Airport connects to Kochi City, then rail and bus continue south. Drivers use Route 321 and signed cape parking; roads are long and winding. A car is useful but requires careful daylight planning.
places.season: Spring and autumn are comfortable for the cliff walk. Summer brings heat, humidity and typhoon risk; rough seas and strong winds can close viewpoints. Check local road, bus and weather notices before leaving Nakamura or Tosashimizu.
places.plan: Walk the cape's marked viewpoints and lighthouse area, then visit Kongofukuji before returning to town. Allow 3-5 hours on site and most of a day for transport from Nakamura. Do not approach cliff edges in high wind or wet weather.

contactSource.title: Visit Kochi: Cape Ashizuri

places.stay: Stay in Tosashimizu near the cape for a relaxed morning and sunset, or near Nakamura Station if relying on the limited bus network.
places.cost: The cape paths and viewpoints are generally free; transport, parking, lodging and some temple facilities cost extra. Confirm current local bus schedules and any weather closures.
points: Cape Ashizuri Park

places.name: Oboke Gorge by river
places.narrative: Oboke Gorge is a close-up encounter with the Yoshino River, where white rock walls squeeze around clear green water. A sightseeing boat reveals the scale from below: cliffs rise directly from the channel and the current traces the gorge's folded geology. The nearby JR Oboke Station sits on the mountain railway line, while Koboke extends the river scenery farther downstream. Spring foliage and autumn leaves change the colour of the slopes; in summer the river feels cooler than the road above. Boat service depends on weather and river conditions, and the station-to-boat walk is longer than it appears on a map. Use the timetable, allow time for the uphill return and never approach the water outside marked access points. Pair the gorge with a local onsen or Iya Valley only if transport allows.
places.access: JR Oboke Station is on the Dosan Line from Awa-Ikeda or Kochi; the sightseeing boat area is about a 20-30 minute walk, with bus or taxi options limited. Takamatsu and Kochi airports connect to the rail corridor. Drivers use National Route 32 and designated parking. Check train and bus frequencies before choosing the station walk or a cross-valley itinerary.
places.season: Spring green and autumn foliage are especially attractive. Boat trips operate in suitable weather and can stop during strong winds or unsafe river conditions. Summer is humid; winter can be cold in the gorge. Check the operator on the day.
places.plan: Walk from JR Oboke Station or arrange a local ride to the boat pier, take the 30-minute sightseeing cruise, then visit a safe roadside viewpoint or continue by rail toward Koboke. Allow 3-5 hours. Avoid combining distant Iya stops without confirmed transport.

contactSource.title: Tokushima official Oboke and Koboke Gorge guide

places.stay: Stay around Oboke or Awa-Ikeda for rail access, or choose an Iya Valley inn if you have arranged transport and a longer mountain itinerary.
places.cost: The sightseeing boat is ticketed; rail, bus, taxi and parking are separate. Boat operation is weather dependent; confirm current fares and last departure.

Oboke Gorge boat pier

places.name: Konpira-san's long climb
places.narrative: The climb to Konpira-san begins in a lively town of udon shops and souvenir stalls, then becomes a stairway through forest, shrine buildings and changing views. The main shrine sits 785 stone steps above the approach; the inner shrine adds another demanding ascent. Visitors who reach the upper precinct are rewarded with a sense of arrival earned one landing at a time. Take breaks, carry water and treat the stairs as a strenuous walk rather than a short photo stop. At the foot of the hill, Kanamaruza, Japan's oldest surviving kabuki theater, offers a striking change of scale and history. Spring and autumn are best for climbing comfortably. The route is steep and not suitable for every visitor; access assistance requires advance arrangements through official channels.
places.access: JR Kotohira Station and Kotoden Kotohira Station are both about a 10-minute walk from the shrine approach. Takamatsu Airport connects by bus to Kotohira; rail links through Takamatsu and Okayama serve other cities. Drivers use town parking, then continue on foot. A limited vehicle-access assistance option requires advance reservation; do not drive up without authorization.
places.season: Spring and autumn are comfortable for the stair climb. Summer heat makes the exposed lower approach tiring; winter can be chilly on the upper steps. Shrine hours, events and assistance reservations should be checked before arrival.
places.plan: Walk the Omotesando approach, climb to the main shrine and return at a pace that suits your fitness; add the inner shrine only if time and energy allow. Allow 3-5 hours. Finish at Kanamaruza. There are 785 steps to the main shrine and 1,368 to the inner shrine.
places.contact: Kotohira Tourism and Community Development Association

contactSource.title: Kotohira Tourism Association contact details

places.stay: Stay near Kotohira Station or the shrine approach for an early start; onsen hotels in the town make a recovery night especially welcome.
places.cost: The main shrine approach is free; museums, theater visits, transport and optional assistance services may cost. Confirm current hours and any reservation rules.

places.name: Beppu, steam rising
places.narrative: Beppu's hot springs are visible before they are felt: steam rises from alleys, rooflines and drains across the Kannawa district. The Jigoku, or hells, are geothermal features to observe, not bathing pools; cobalt Umi Jigoku, red Chinoike Jigoku and the geyser at Tatsumaki Jigoku each show a different expression of volcanic heat. Five sites cluster around Kannawa and are walkable between; the two Kamegawa-area hells sit about three kilometers away and need a bus or car. This is the key to an enjoyable visit: group the sites by area instead of following a scattered checklist. Autumn and winter make the steam especially vivid, though the district is worth visiting year-round. Respect barriers, avoid touching hot water and choose a separate onsen for bathing.
places.access: JR Beppu Station connects by limited express and local trains to Oita, Fukuoka and other Kyushu cities; Oita Airport buses reach Beppu. Kamenoi buses from Beppu Station serve Umi Jigoku and Kannawa, around 20 minutes. By car, Beppu IC is a short drive; each hell has parking. Use a bus or car between Kannawa and the Kamegawa pair rather than walking the three-kilometer gap.
places.season: The steam is striking in cool autumn and winter air; spring is comfortable for walking. Summer is hot and humid. Hells are open year-round on published schedules, but individual sites and bus routes may change hours.
places.plan: Visit Umi Jigoku, Kamado Jigoku and nearby Kannawa sites on foot, then ride a bus or drive to Chinoike Jigoku and Tatsumaki Jigoku. Allow 4-6 hours. These are hot-spring viewing sites, not bathing pools; choose a separate bathhouse for an onsen experience.

contactSource.title: Beppu Jigoku Association official access

places.stay: Stay in Kannawa for the steam district and nearby baths, or near Beppu Station for transport, restaurants and easy onward rail connections.
places.cost: The seven hells are ticketed individually or by shared pass; buses, parking and bathing facilities are separate. Confirm current shared-ticket validity and operating hours.
points: Umi Jigoku

Kamado Jigoku

Chinoike Jigoku

places.name: Yakushima, ancient green
places.narrative: Yakushima's forest feels ancient because the island makes time visible: rain-darkened cedar roots, moss-soft stones and trees whose trunks hold centuries of weather. Shiratani Unsuikyo is a compelling first walk, with marked trails through cedar and moss forest and optional longer loops for prepared hikers. It is not a theme-park path; rain, slippery roots and steep sections change the effort quickly. The island also has waterfalls, coastal settlements and the Yakusugi Museum, so a thoughtful visit balances mountain forest with a lower-elevation stop. The famous Jomon Sugi hike is a separate, strenuous full-day undertaking and should not be added casually to this short route. Spring and autumn are often comfortable, but rain is possible in every season. Check trail and bus status, bring layers and carry out everything you bring in.
places.access: Flights connect Yakushima Airport with Kagoshima, while ferries and high-speed boats serve Miyanoura and Anbo ports. Local buses and rental cars connect villages; Shiratani Unsuikyo trailhead is reached by bus from Miyanoura when services operate. Kagoshima Airport and Kagoshima Chuo Station are the main gateways. Bus frequencies are limited, so check return times or arrange a car before hiking.
places.season: Yakushima is rainy year-round. Spring and autumn are comfortable for hiking, while winter brings cold mountain conditions and summer brings heat and heavy rain. Trail access can close because of weather; check the town and forestry notices on the day.
places.plan: Choose a marked Shiratani Unsuikyo loop suited to your fitness, then visit the Yakusugi Museum or a nearby coast viewpoint on a separate transport leg. Allow 4-7 hours for the forest walk. Jomon Sugi is a strenuous full-day hike requiring an early start and separate preparation.
places.contact: Yakushima Tourism Association, Miyanoura Information Office

contactSource.title: Yakushima official hiking and visitor information 2026

places.stay: Stay in Miyanoura for port access or Anbo for southern routes and the Yakusugi Museum; reserve a night before and after long hikes to protect your schedule.
places.cost: Shiratani Unsuikyo requires a conservation cooperation fee; buses, flights, ferries, guides and lodging are separate. Check current trail fees and access restrictions.
points: Shiratani Unsuikyo trailhead
Check the trail notice, weather and return transport before starting; choose the route length that matches your daylight.
Yayoisugi trail
Follow the marked loop among cedar trees and mossy forest; roots and stones can be slippery after rain.
Moss forest paths
Use official marked routes only and avoid stepping on fragile moss or leaving the trail for photographs.
Yakusugi Museum
